name: Ruth Henderson

biography.name: Ruth Henderson

background.family: Lives with parents and a younger sibling on a small working farm.
background.finances: Income varies seasonally; household is stable and maintains a contingency fund.
background.cultureLanguages: English; family participates in agricultural and church community events.
background.school: Small public high school; some advanced courses delivered remotely.
background.accessOpportunities: Farm equipment, regional library, online courses, and periodic city trips.

timeline.story: In 2014, Ruth followed a parent during animal feeding and asked where the feed had been before arriving in sacks. She liked tracing everyday objects backward through imagined journeys and drawing those journeys on long strips of paper.

At six, she started flute lessons with a visiting instructor. During 2017, she enjoyed finding notes by ear but resisted counting practice repetitions, claiming that playing one phrase carefully should matter more than playing it ten times.

In 2018, Ruth became curious about stars after an overnight family campout. She borrowed books beyond her reading level and accepted help with difficult passages, while remaining uninterested in the public presentation her teacher suggested making afterward.

During 2020, home routines stayed fairly predictable. Ruth completed online assignments around farm chores and began baking bread, treating differences in dough temperature as a puzzle rather than assuming a disappointing loaf meant she was bad at cooking.

At twelve, Ruth took a remote algebra course and liked its clean symbolic steps. In 2023, she joined a regional music ensemble, discovering that she could enjoy a group even without becoming especially close to every member.

Across 2024 and 2025, she helped maintain farm records, read popular physics, and practiced flute. She liked abstract questions but disliked the expectation that enjoying science required her to enter competitions or announce a grand plan.

At sixteen in 2026, Ruth is comparing Texas community-college classes with a short university physics program. She wants to learn difficult material while staying connected to home, and she is uncertain whether she wants a long academic pathway or simply a stronger understanding.

ambitions: Try a course with hands-on experiments
She imagines a settled adult life near open space, with reliable work, music, and time to read.
struggles: Understates her questions when adults push ambitions

Quantities, farm records, systematic recipes and scientific reading support related observations and checking, with formal labs still new.
She prefers quiet competence to public showcases, commercial persuasion and urgent response.

Curiosity about physics does not establish every laboratory activity or a long academic career. No direct preference is established for these specific activities; Unsure preserves that gap rather than inferring enjoyment from exposure or identity.

Scientific explanation and repeatable testing are attractive, while direct customer service and prominent teaching are less established. Abstract inquiry itself has real appeal. Middle ratings for unfamiliar domains are tentative curiosity, not claims of experience.

Symbolic steps and quantity records justify independent numbers; systematic recipe changes count as some science experience, while laboratory methods still need support. New/supported marks limited practice; an independent response describes a familiar task, not a measured aptitude.

Quiet competence and familiar ensemble participation support mixed company with a steady rhythm. She considers college physics and community-college classes but explicitly questions a long academic pathway.
Physics questions and controlled bread variations motivate trying hands-on experiments she has not yet accessed. These are exploratory preferences, with no inferred job commitment.
